question: Which way do negative inventory layer depths project, and where can stereo correction survive native matrix assembly?
claim: The verified Steam matrix routine produces homogeneous W=C+worldZ, so negative native Z is closer. It clears horizontal projection offsets before multiplication; final output correction survives that native calculation.
method: Offline PE landmark checks and Unicorn 2.1.4 execution of unmodified Steam CalcTransMat3D plus its native matrix-multiply callee. Four Z fixtures with known centre projection, explicit return address and callee-saved register control. Reproduce with Python tools/re/verify_inventory_stereo.py. No game process was launched or instrumented.

identity.reason: SHA-256, x64 image base, vtable target and instruction anchors checked against Steam bytes.

instrument.reason: All four bounded emulations return correctly and preserve seeded callee-saved register; projected centre and W match independently calculated fixtures.

control.reason: Z=0 gives W=C; both negative and positive offsets produce expected monotonic opposite changes. C++ zero-depth test is bit exact.

scene.reason: Explicit synthetic native matrix fixtures using previously captured PDA view basis; not an in-game scene.
